text.p: Italian Btp bond futures ended firmer, though off session highs, with the market reassured that domestic political tension appeared to recede for the moment.

After a gloomy morning also linked to technical problems on the MTS secondary bond market, the trend was reversed when the leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation, Fausto Bertinotti, said that his differences with Italy's centre-left government over employment policy had been resolved.

"The stalemate and division that had arisen within the (governing) majority has been unblocked," Bertinotti said in a statement. Also, opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said he thought it was highly unlikely the government would fall.

"The forces of the left might argue, but they will never let this coalition fall," Berlusconi told a gathering of foreign reporters. "It would be very difficult for this government to fall," he added.
The June Btp Liffe contract jumped to a session high of 126.30 and the lira firmed against the mark. But in the cash market, the November 2006 Btp slipped a touch.

Dealers said they expected the June future to retest resistance around 126.25 on Friday. "We saw a real change in climate this afternoon with renewed foreign buying," one dealer said. The spread over 10-year bunds narrowed to 194 after early touching 200 basis points.
